site.name: codekite
site.summary: codekite-clone Fictional cloud CI/CD service "CodeKite CI" marketing site, focused on the pricing-page usage calculator. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Short landing: hero (YAML code example on the right), 3 feature cards, CTA to pricing | | `pricing.html` | Main page: 3 plan cards (Free / Team / Enterprise) + usage calculator (three slider+number pairs linked two-way: build minutes / concurrency / storage + ARM / macOS / GPU runner checkboxes); right-side sticky monthly total + recommended-plan badge + line-item cost breakdown; below: 16-row plan comparison table; 10-question FAQ accordion; trusted-logo row; 4-column footer | | `docs.html` | Placeholder quickstart page (one YAML example) |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full codekite system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The pricing experience communicates its value proposition clearly, and the calculator provides immediate live feedback with a recommended plan and detailed breakdown. However, several key conversion controls are styled like primary actions but behave as dead ends, which undermines trust and makes the page feel less actionable than it looks. The calculator also has accessibility and touch-target issues, especially on mobile, and lower-page disclosure/FAQ interactions appear non-functional from the tested states. Coverage is broad across index, pricing, and docs, but a few adjacent links and some calculator features remain untested, so there may be additional navigation dead-ends beyond those observed.

exploration_plan.goal: Thoroughly validate CodeKite’s primary pricing calculator flow, supporting plan/FAQ/comparison content, and adjacent navigation paths across desktop and mobile.
exploration_plan.summary: Start from the landing page to confirm the main conversion paths into pricing and docs, then spend most of the run on pricing.html where the interactive calculator, plan selection, monthly total, and recommendation logic live. After that, verify adjacent informational content on docs.html and return to pricing for deeper validation of the comparison table, FAQ accordion, and footer links. Repeat the critical pricing checks in a mobile viewport, with special attention to small tap targets and the calculator’s two-way linked controls.
assumptions: The pricing page is the primary product experience and contains the most meaningful interactive behavior in the site.
The three slider/number pairs on pricing.html are linked two-way and should stay synchronized when either control is changed.
The right-side sticky monthly total and recommended-plan badge update live based on calculator inputs.
Some footer and nav links are placeholders or external-style destinations and may not navigate to unique internal pages.
Mobile exploration should emphasize usability and control sizing rather than deep content variation, since only three HTML pages are known.
risk_hotspots: pricing.html calculator: three linked slider + number pairs for build minutes, concurrency, and storage
pricing.html add-on checkboxes for ARM / macOS / GPU runners and their effect on total cost
pricing.html sticky monthly total, recommended-plan badge, and line-item breakdown
pricing.html plan cards and CTA buttons: Free / Team / Enterprise actions
pricing.html 16-row comparison table and 10-question FAQ accordion
index.html and pricing.html small tap targets in header/footer on mobile
docs.html quickstart page: ensure the YAML example and nav links behave as expected

phases.title: Landing page entry and navigation
phases.objective: Validate the homepage messaging and the main routes into pricing and docs before focusing on the calculator.
key_checks: Confirm the hero CTA pair routes to pricing and docs as expected.
Verify top navigation links for Product, Pricing, Docs, Sign in, and Start free trial are present and usable.
Check whether the page has any broken or placeholder links beyond the visible marketing paths.
exit_criteria: Pricing and docs entry points have been exercised from the landing page.
No unexpected navigation failures or obvious broken primary CTAs are observed.

phases.title: Pricing page core calculator
phases.objective: Stress the primary pricing flow and confirm that editable controls, cost updates, and plan recommendations stay consistent.
key_checks: Interact with each slider and its paired number input to confirm two-way synchronization.
Test a few meaningful states for build minutes, concurrency, and storage, including low, mid, and high values.
Toggle ARM, macOS, and GPU runner checkboxes and verify their impact on the estimate and line items.
Observe whether the sticky monthly total and recommended-plan badge update correctly after each change.
Check for any formatting issues, stale totals, or mismatched labels in the cost breakdown.
exit_criteria: All three linked input pairs have been manipulated in both directions.
At least one changed state has been validated for each add-on checkbox.
The monthly total and recommended-plan behavior have been observed under multiple input combinations.

phases.title: Pricing plans, comparison, and FAQ
phases.objective: Validate the surrounding pricing content that supports purchase decisions and common questions.
key_checks: Open and inspect the plan cards for Free, Team, and Enterprise, including their CTAs.
Scan the 16-row comparison table for alignment, readability, and consistency with the plan cards.
Exercise several FAQ accordion items to confirm expand/collapse behavior and content clarity.
Check whether repeated CTAs such as Get started, Start trial, and Talk to sales feel consistent with plan positioning.
exit_criteria: Each plan card has been reviewed.
Multiple FAQ items have been expanded and collapsed successfully.
The comparison table has been visually checked for structure or overflow issues.

phases.title: Docs adjacency and back-navigation
phases.objective: Confirm the adjacent docs experience and ensure the site supports a reasonable informational detour from pricing.
key_checks: Verify the quickstart content loads and the YAML example is readable.
Check the header navigation back to Pricing and other top-level pages.
Confirm the docs page is consistent with the marketing site's tone and does not introduce broken states.
exit_criteria: Docs page content and navigation are verified.
Any path back to pricing has been exercised cleanly.

phases.title: Mobile viewport regression pass
phases.objective: Repeat the most important conversion and calculator checks on a mobile viewport, emphasizing touch usability and layout stability.
key_checks: Recheck header navigation and primary CTAs for tap usability on small screens.
Repeat core calculator interactions on pricing, including at least one slider/number pair and one checkbox toggle.
Verify the sticky total, plan cards, and FAQ remain usable without clipping or overlap.
Note any small tap target or spacing problems that hinder mobile use.
exit_criteria: Critical pricing interactions have been confirmed on mobile.
Mobile-specific layout or tap target issues have been documented where visible.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages: index.html, pricing.html, and docs.html.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the homepage CTAs, pricing calculator inputs, add-on checkboxes, plan CTAs, comparison table, FAQ accordion, docs quickstart content, and key header/footer navigation links.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the pricing calculator, main CTA, and one or two supporting navigation/content checks in a mobile viewport, with explicit attention to the small tap targets already flagged by prescan.

notes: Prescan already indicates no console or network errors; prioritize interaction/state validation and responsive usability over error hunting.
Several footer/social-style links on the landing page are placeholders (#), so treat them as likely non-navigational unless the run reveals otherwise.
Because the pricing page already shows missing input labels in prescan, pay special attention to accessibility and clarity around the calculator controls.

findings.user_goal: Start a trial or proceed from the pricing page with confidence
findings.problem: Primary pricing CTAs on the Free and Team plans look like real conversion actions but do nothing when tapped or clicked.
findings.evidence: On mobile, clicking "Get started" and "Start trial" caused no visible text or URL change; both stayed on `pricing.html#` with no state change. The final observation also shows these CTAs use `href="#"`.
findings.why_it_matters: Users who intend to begin onboarding may think they are continuing, but the page gives no destination or next step. That breaks the conversion funnel and can feel deceptive.
findings.suggestion: Make the plan CTAs navigate to a real signup/trial flow, or if they are intentionally placeholders, label them clearly and replace the button styling with a non-clickable or explanatory pattern.

findings.user_goal: Understand whether clicking FAQ items reveals answers or useful details
findings.problem: FAQ/accordion-style rows appear interactive, but clicking them only changes the URL fragment and does not visibly expand content.
findings.evidence: On mobile, clicking "Overview" changed the URL to `pricing.html#` with no answer text or state change. Earlier trajectory chunks show the same behavior for "Overview" and "Changelog", with no visible disclosure after clicking.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may rely on the FAQ for purchase reassurance. If the control doesn’t visibly open, they lose confidence and cannot get answers to common objections.
findings.suggestion: Ensure each FAQ row expands in place with a clear open/closed state, or if these are anchor links, label them as such and scroll to substantive content.

findings.user_goal: Estimate pricing accurately using the usage calculator
findings.problem: The core calculator inputs lack labels/accessible names, making the main pricing tool hard to understand and use with assistive tech or on small screens.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flagged multiple "missing_input_label" issues for the range and number fields, and the trajectory notes that the calculator inputs lack visible labels/accessible names in the DOM summary.
findings.why_it_matters: The calculator is the centerpiece of the pricing page. Unlabeled controls make it harder to tell which field controls which cost driver, increasing errors and frustration.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit labels for each slider/number pair and ensure labels are programmatically associated so the values and controls are understandable to screen readers and sighted users alike.

findings.user_goal: Tap navigation and pricing controls comfortably on a phone
findings.problem: Several top-nav and footer/header targets are below mobile tap-target guidance, and the add-on checkboxes are extremely small.
findings.evidence: The mobile observation lists low tap-target sizes for Pricing (47x21), Start free trial (125x41), and brand/nav items such as CodeKite. The calculator add-on checkboxes are only 13x13px, and the page shows repeated small-target warnings in the layout summary.
findings.why_it_matters: Small targets increase accidental taps and make the page frustrating to operate on touch devices, especially for frequently used navigation and pricing options.
findings.suggestion: Increase hit areas to at least mobile guidance sizes, add padding around nav links, and make checkbox rows tap-friendly by enlarging the clickable label area.
findings.source_hint: pricing.html; header nav and add-on checkboxes `ux-13`–`ux-15`

findings.user_goal: Move from pricing to onboarding or sales contact with a meaningful next step
findings.problem: The page visually emphasizes conversion actions, but several of them are dead-end placeholders rather than real destinations.
findings.evidence: The Team CTA "Start trial" and the Free CTA "Get started" both failed to navigate or change visible state. The same `href="#"` pattern appears on the sticky top CTA as well.
findings.why_it_matters: When users click a prominent CTA and nothing happens, it creates confusion and reduces trust in the rest of the pricing flow.
findings.suggestion: Replace placeholder links with actual destinations, or clearly mark them as demo-only if they are not meant to convert users yet.

findings.user_goal: Use the site header/footer to reach related information
findings.problem: Some non-primary links behave like placeholders, which weakens the sense that the footer/navigation is reliable.
findings.evidence: The footer About link on the homepage only changed the URL to `index.html#` without any content change, and the session memory notes other placeholder-like routes such as Careers, Security, Blog, and Status on different pages.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect navigation links to lead somewhere meaningful. Dead-end links can make the site feel unfinished and reduce confidence in the brand.
findings.suggestion: Either route these links to substantive pages or visually mark them as unavailable so users do not expect real content.
findings.source_hint: index.html footer About; related placeholder links in nav/footer

findings.user_goal: Read and interact with the pricing page on a mobile device
findings.problem: Multiple key interactive elements are below comfortable mobile touch sizes, even when the layout is otherwise readable.
findings.evidence: The mobile screenshot and layout warnings show the Pricing link at 47x21px, the brand link at 28x21px, and the start trial button at 125x41px; earlier chunks also flagged header items below 44px guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Tiny targets make it easy to miss taps and increase interaction cost, especially for users with motor impairments or when browsing one-handed.
findings.suggestion: Rework the header into a more touch-friendly mobile pattern with larger vertical spacing and fewer compressed inline links.

findings.user_goal: Compare plans and understand the pricing structure
findings.problem: The page is strong on content density, but some lower sections remain partially clipped while scrolling, which can interrupt scanning on mobile.
findings.evidence: The recent mobile scroll notes say the FAQ accordion cards were visible but still partially extending below the viewport, and the sticky header remains present while users scroll lower content.
findings.why_it_matters: When lower-page content is clipped, users may miss questions or think the page has ended, especially on smaller screens.
findings.suggestion: Give lower sections more vertical breathing room or reduce sticky header intrusion so the FAQ and comparison table can be scanned without partial clipping.
